image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a Red Lionfish (Pterois volitans) swimming in an aquarium environment. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical stripes, large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays, and prominent dorsal spines. The background consists of blurred rocky reef structures and coral.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large head with prominent eyes and wide mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible on the right side of the image. The eye is distinct and prominent, and the mouth structure is consistent with lionfish anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears laterally compressed as expected for a scorpaenid fish. Proportions relative to the fins are accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brightly striped coloration in red, white, brown, or black bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows distinct, high-contrast vertical banding in reddish-brown and white, matching the species description perfectly.

While lionfish have small scales, they are not individually resolvable at this magnification and distance. The texture appears smooth/skin-like due to resolution limits, making this checkpoint untestable rather than absent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal fin with numerous elongated venomous spines that fan outward like mane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal spines are clearly visible along the top ridge, fanning out distinctly. They appear structurally sound and separate from one another.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are fully extended and display the characteristic fan shape with individual rays clearly defined and separated.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pelvic fins are visible beneath the body, showing the typical elongated spine structure associated with the species.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Pterois volitans vs other scorpionfish) and verify fine-grained taxonomic features.
To ensure the thin, elongated fin rays do not merge with the background or each other (common AI artifact in complex transparent structures).
To detect subtle texture anomalies in the skin pattern or background blur consistency.
To verify the 3D volume of the fish against the 2D background, ensuring no 'flatness' or grounding errors.

focus_areas: Integrity of thin fin rays (no fusion/melting)
Consistency of stripe patterns across body curvature
Separation of dorsal spines from background
Anatomical correctness of fin attachment points
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the dorsal and pectoral fin rays. AI generators often struggle with maintaining sharp, distinct endpoints for thin, semi-transparent structures against complex backgrounds. Verify if any rays fade unnaturally or merge with the rock/coral behind them. Also, check if the stripe pattern wraps logically around the 3D form of the fish without sudden discontinuities.
